text:
Alex K: Draft PRD up for 'Docs-driven rollout policies' — linking in thread. Goal: make docs the spec so eng can implement from examples + acceptance criteria. Need agreement on MVP scope and launch criteria before I move to final PRD.

Maria P: skimmed. +1 on docs-as-spec. Two immediate questions: 1) do we include canary scheduling UI in MVP? 2) do we require audit log export for Private customers at launch?

Alex K: Quick answers: 1) MVP = API + CLI for canary rollouts, UI later (v1). 2) Audit log export = must-have for Private, optional for Hosted. Will call that out in acceptance criteria.

Danielle R: I'll own the docs-as-spec pattern. Plan: each feature page must include a "Quickstart" (runnable example), "Acceptance criteria" (pass/fail), and an "Edge cases & rollout notes" section. Anyone object?

Samir T: no objections. A couple of notes from infra: we need a clear compatibility table for model variants (quantized vs fp16) because fallback behavior depends on it. Add a small matrix in the docs.

John L: From solutions/customer asks: Acme wants canaries + per-tenant rollback hooks and audit payloads delivered to customer S3. Can we scope that into Dedicated/Private only for MVP and note Hosted as roadmap item?

Alex K: Yes — Dedicated/Private: per-tenant rollback hooks + S3 export for audit. Hosted: provide webhook audit sink + managed retention for launch, S3 export in v1. I'll mark that in the PRD with explicit acceptance tests.

Priya S: Add acceptance criteria to verify legal/regulatory metadata is present in audit logs (user id, request id, model id, timestamp, region). Customer compliance teams will ask.

Danielle R: I'll draft the acceptance criteria. Proposal (short):
- AC1: Canaries can be created via API/CLI and target percentage rollout.
- AC2: Rollout execution records every decision event to audit log with required metadata.
- AC3: Rollbacks can be triggered via API/CLI and revert traffic within 30s under normal load.
- AC4: Quickstart reproduces canary creation + rollback end-to-end in the docs using a local dev model (scriptable).
- AC5: Compatibility matrix present with clear fallback rules; tests included in the engineering test plan.

Maria P: For AC3, ops: 30s is optimistic for cold KV caches. Can we change to 60s SLO with effort to hit 30s in 90% of cases? Also add non-functional acceptance criteria for token-level latency regression (<5% p50 change).

Alex K: Updated: rollback SLO = 60s, target 30s for warmed caches. Add latency regression guardrails as AC6.

Danielle R: I'll add a small runnable quickstart. Draft snippet below — please sanity-check.

```bash
# quickstart: create a canary rollout (local dev)
redwood rollouts create --model rwd-embed-v2 --policy canary --percent 10 --name quickstart-test
redwood rollouts promote --name quickstart-test --percent 50
# simulate a failure and rollback
redwood rollouts rollback --name quickstart-test --force
```

Maria P: CLI looks fine. For tests, let's add an automated e2e that: 1) creates a canary, 2) sends synthetic traffic, 3) asserts route percentages, 4) triggers rollback and asserts traffic shifts. We can reuse the rate-limiter harness.

John L: Also include example of webhook audit sink payload in docs. Something like:

```json
{"event":"rollout.change","tenant":"acme","user":"ops@acme.com","model":"rwd-embed-v2","decision":"promote","percent":50,"ts":"2026-03-01T12:00:00Z"}
```

Priya S: +request: include a line item for data residency — customers must be able to pin audit exports to region. Mark as requirement for Private/Dedicated.

Alex K: Agree. I'll add two launch criteria: region-pin for audit exports (Private/Dedicated) and webhook sinks for Hosted.

Danielle R: Timeline check: If eng commits to a 2-week implementation spike (api + minimal tests) we can have docs + quickstart ready in week 3 for a staged review. Is that realistic?

Maria P: Yes, 2-week spike + 2 weeks for hardening and tests. Tentative milestone: spike start 1748100000 (ETA next week).

Alex K: Ok — action items: Danielle to produce docs PR with examples and ACs by week 3; Maria to schedule spike and assign eng owners; John to provide customer webhook example and CS acceptance; Priya to confirm compliance checklist items. I'll update the PRD with scoped MVP and v1 backlog.

ci-bot: new file created: /prs/1748001234-prd-rollout-policies.md : PR opened by @Alex K : https://git.internal/redwood/prs/4321

Alex K: Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll lock MVP as API+CLI canaries, audit webhook for Hosted, S3 export + rollback hooks for Dedicated/Private, and UI deferred to v1. Please add any final objections in-thread by EOD. :thumbsup:
